tasks.title: swap_remove
tasks.statement: Write remove_all_even(v: &mut Vec<i32>): remove all even numbers in linear time without preserving order, using swap_remove. (The check is by the sum and the count of the remaining elements.)
tasks.hint: Do not increment i after swap_remove — a new element is already in that place.

tasks.title: split_off
tasks.statement: Write split_at_value(v: &mut Vec<i32>, x: i32) -> Vec<i32>: cut off the tail of v starting from the first element equal to x (if x is absent, return an empty vector) and return it.
tasks.hint: v.split_off(i) leaves the first i elements in v.

tasks.title: dedup_by_key
tasks.statement: Write unique_by_len(words: &mut Vec<String>): keep only the first word of each run of consecutive words with the same length in characters (dedup_by_key).
tasks.hint: dedup_by_key removes adjacent elements with the same key.

tasks.title: Extract by a condition
tasks.statement: Write take_evens(v: &mut Vec<i32>) -> Vec<i32>: return all even numbers (in the original order) and remove them from v. Use retain and accumulate into a separate vector.
tasks.hint: retain calls the closure in order — you can accumulate inside it.

tasks.title: Rotating a slice
tasks.statement: Write rotate(v: &mut [i32], k: usize): a cyclic shift right by k positions in place (rotate_right; k may exceed the length).
tasks.hint: rotate_right panics when k > len, so take k % len.

tasks.title: Maximum in a window
tasks.statement: Write window_max(v: &[i32], k: usize) -> Vec<i32>: the maximum in each window of k consecutive elements (k > 0; if k > len — empty). In linear time (a VecDeque holds the indices of candidates), on 200000 elements.
tasks.hint: A queue of decreasing values: drop the tail if it is not greater than the new one.

tasks.title: Counting-out game on a deque
tasks.statement: Write last_standing(names: &[&str], k: usize) -> String: going around the circle, every k-th person drops out; return the name of the last one. Use VecDeque and rotate_left.
tasks.hint: q.rotate_left(k - 1), then pop_front.

tasks.title: Round-robin scheduler
tasks.statement: Write round_robin(tasks: &[(&str, u32)], quantum: u32) -> Vec<String>: each task in turn gets quantum units; return the completion order (names) as a list. VecDeque.
tasks.hint: If it is not finished — to the back of the queue with the remainder.

tasks.title: Common elements
tasks.statement: Write common_sorted(a: &[i32], b: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>: the intersection of a and b without repeats in ascending order (HashSet).
tasks.hint: Two sets and intersection.

tasks.title: Subset
tasks.statement: Write can_make(note: &str, magazine: &str) -> bool: are the letters in magazine enough to cut out note (each letter once; compare as is, ignore spaces). A HashMap of counters.
tasks.hint: The magazine's letter counters decrease as you cut out.

tasks.title: Ranks in ascending order
tasks.statement: Write ranks(v: &[i32]) -> Vec<usize>: for each element, its index (from 0) among the distinct values in ascending order (coordinate compression): [10, 5, 10, 7] → [2, 0, 2, 1]. Use BTreeSet.
tasks.hint: BTreeSet gives sorted unique values; binary_search gives the index.

tasks.title: Nearest values
tasks.statement: Write nearest(sorted: &BTreeSet<i32>, x: i32) -> (Option<i32>, Option<i32>): the largest value not greater than x and the smallest value not less than x (range methods).
tasks.hint: range(..=x).next_back() and range(x..).next()

tasks.title: Events in order
tasks.statement: Write timeline(events: &[(u32, &str)]) -> Vec<String>: output the events (time, name) in time order; for equal times, the names joined with «/» in insertion order. Strings like «5: a/b». BTreeMap.
tasks.hint: entry(t).or_default().push(n); BTreeMap iterates in ascending order.

tasks.title: Priority tasks
tasks.statement: Write process(tasks: &[(u32, &str)]) -> Vec<String>: tasks (priority, name) run from the smallest priority (number) to the largest; for equal ones — in insertion order. Use BTreeMap<u32, VecDeque<String>> and pop_first.
tasks.hint: pop_first gives the pair with the smallest key.

tasks.title: Top-k with a heap
tasks.statement: Write top_k(v: &[i32], k: usize) -> Vec<i32>: the k largest in descending order, using a min-heap of size k (BinaryHeap<Reverse<i32>>) — for 300000 elements and k = 5.
tasks.hint: If the heap holds more than k, remove the smallest.

tasks.title: Merging k lists
tasks.statement: Write merge_k(lists: &[Vec<i32>]) -> Vec<i32>: merge sorted lists into one sorted list, using BinaryHeap<Reverse<(i32, usize, usize)>> (value, list number, index).
tasks.hint: The heap always holds one candidate from each list.

tasks.title: Running median
tasks.statement: Write running_median(v: &[i32]) -> Vec<f64>: after each element, the median of everything read so far (two heaps: the lower one is a max-heap, the upper one a min-heap).
tasks.hint: The heap sizes differ by at most one.

tasks.title: Dijkstra with a heap
tasks.statement: Write dijkstra(n: usize, edges: &[(usize, usize, u32)], src: usize) -> Vec<Option<u32>>: shortest distances from src in a directed graph of n vertices; unreachable ones — None. A min-heap; a graph of 20000 vertices.
tasks.hint: Skip stale entries in the heap: d > dist[u].

tasks.title: Palindrome with a deque
tasks.statement: Write is_pal(s: &str) -> bool: is the string a palindrome (letters and digits only, case-insensitive), comparing characters from both ends of a VecDeque.
tasks.hint: Compare pairs from pop_front and pop_back.

tasks.title: Mini LRU
tasks.statement: The struct Lru { cap: usize, order: VecDeque<String>, map: HashMap<String, i32> }. Implement new(cap), get(&mut self, k: &str) -> Option<i32> (an access makes the key the freshest) and put(&mut self, k: &str, v: i32) (updating a key also makes it the freshest; on overflow the oldest is removed).
tasks.hint: touch moves the key to the end of the order; the oldest is at the front.

tasks.title: Pairs with a sum
tasks.statement: Write count_pairs(v: &[i32], target: i32) -> usize: how many index pairs i < j have v[i] + v[j] = target (a HashMap of frequencies, one pass) — on 200000 elements.
tasks.hint: Before adding x to the map, look up its partner.

tasks.title: Grouping by first letter
tasks.statement: Write group_by_first(words: &[&str]) -> BTreeMap<char, Vec<String>>: words grouped by first letter (lowercase); empty strings are skipped; inside groups — in ascending order.
tasks.hint: entry(letter).or_default().push(…); then sort.

tasks.title: Most frequent
tasks.statement: Write most_common(v: &[i32]) -> Option<i32>: the most frequent value; on a tie — the smallest. For an empty input — None. A HashMap and one pass over the map.
tasks.hint: max_by with the same comparison, with the key in reverse order.

tasks.title: Do not reallocate
tasks.statement: Write squares(n: usize) -> Vec<u64>: the squares of 0…n−1, reserving memory in advance (with_capacity) — after filling, capacity() must be equal to n.
tasks.hint: Vec::with_capacity(n)

tasks.title: concat and join
tasks.statement: Write flatten_join(rows: &[Vec<&str>]) -> String: join the strings of each subgroup with spaces, and separate the groups with « | » (the join method on a slice).
tasks.hint: Two joins: the inner and the outer.

tasks.title: binary_search_by
tasks.statement: Write find_user(users: &[(u32, &str)], id: u32) -> Option<&str>: users is sorted by id; find the name with binary search (binary_search_by_key).
tasks.hint: binary_search_by_key(&id, |&(i, _)| i)

tasks.title: Sorting matrix rows
tasks.statement: Write sort_rows(m: &mut Vec<Vec<i32>>): sort each row in ascending order, and then sort the rows among themselves lexicographically.
tasks.hint: Vec<Vec<i32>> already compares lexicographically.

tasks.title: Visited states
tasks.statement: Write steps_to_cycle(start: u32) -> usize: the sequence x → (x·x + 1) mod 1000; how many steps until the first repeated value (a HashSet of visited values; start counts as visited at time 0).
tasks.hint: insert returns false when the value was already there.

tasks.title: Heap sort
tasks.statement: Write heap_sort(v: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>: sort in ascending order through a BinaryHeap (from + into_sorted_vec).
tasks.hint: into_sorted_vec returns ascending order.

tasks.title: When a list, when a vector
tasks.statement: Write move_front(v: &mut Vec<i32>, i: usize): move the element at index i to the front of the vector, keeping the order of the rest (remove + insert, or rotate_right on the slice 0..=i).
tasks.hint: v[..=i].rotate_right(1) without copying the whole vector.
